question.value: How and on what timescales is the Fornax cluster galaxy NGC 1436 transitioning from a spiral into a lenticular morphology through environmental interactions?

evidence.quote: We study the evolutionary path of the Fornax cluster galaxy NGC 1436, which is known to be currently transitioning from a spiral into a lenticular morphology.

One of the members of the nearby Fornax galaxy cluster (distance ∼ 20 Mpc; Jensen et al. 2001; Tonry et al. 2001; Blakeslee et al. 2009; Spriggs et al. 2021), NGC 1436 (FCC 290), is a perfect target to study "how" and "how quickly" the evolution of spirals into S0's can happen in dense environments.

findings_qualitative.value: Both the inner and outer discs experienced normal cosmic inside-out evolution until ~5 Gyr ago, a burst of star formation peaking 3-4 Gyr ago, followed by rapid quenching in the outer disc and slow starvation-like decline in the inner disc.

evidence.quote: In summary, our SFH analysis indicates that both the inner and outer disc populations went through three main star-formation phases: (i) a rather typical build up activity and a steady decline in star-formation activity until some 5 Gyr ago, (ii) a burst of star formation peaking between 3 and 4 Gyr ago, and (iii) a final drop in star-formation until present times, gradually reducing it by two orders of magnitude in the inner disc and completely quenching star formation in the outer disc.

claims.hypothesis: NGC 1436 has not experienced any significant tidal or hydrodynamical environmental interactions in the last ~1 Gyr.
claims.experiment: Map and model the HI distribution and kinematics at 11'' and 66'' resolution with MeerKAT and compare with ALMA CO(1-0) distribution and kinematics.
claims.result: The HI is entirely confined to a symmetric ring within the inner star-forming disc with no tails or asymmetries down to 1.3e18 cm^-2, and its kinematics is well-settled and coincident with CO; the orbital time at the disc edge is ~300 Myr.
claims.finding: The cold gas disc is well settled, ruling out strong environmental interactions in the last few orbital times (~1 Gyr).

evidence.quote: Thanks to the combination of high resolution and sensitivity of the MeerKAT data, we find that the H I is entirely confined within the inner star-forming disc, and that its kinematics is coincident with that of the CO. The cold gas disc is now well settled, which suggests that the galaxy has not been affected by any environmental interactions in the last ∼ 1 Gyr.

evidence.loc: 3 MORPHOLOGY AND KINEMATICS OF THE COLD GAS DISC
evidence.quote: Given that the orbital time at the disc's edge is of ∼300 Myr (as derived from the de-projected rotational velocity of ∼130 km s [−][1] at a radius of ∼ 6.7 kpc) we can rule out strong interactions in the last few orbital times, roughly 1 Gyr.

claims.hypothesis: Interactions with the Fornax cluster environment began ~5 Gyr ago, triggering a star formation burst followed by rapid gas stripping in the outer disc and slow starvation in the inner disc.
claims.experiment: Reconstruct non-parametric star formation histories of the inner star-forming and outer quiescent discs by fitting MUSE aperture spectra in elliptical annular sectors using pPXF and GandALF with MILES SSP models.
claims.result: Both discs show a burst of star formation peaking 3-4 Gyr ago (forming ~50% and ~20% of stars in the inner and outer discs), followed by complete quenching in the outer disc and a gradual two-order-of-magnitude decline in the inner disc.
claims.finding: NGC 1436 began interacting with the cluster ~5 Gyr ago; near pericentre (~4 Gyr ago), tidal and/or ram-pressure interactions compressed gas (enhancing SFR) and stripped HI from the outer disc (causing rapid quenching), while halting gas accretion onto the inner disc (causing slow starvation).

evidence.quote: We claim that NGC 1436 has begun to effectively interact with the cluster environment 5 Gyr ago, when a combination of gravitational and hydrodynamical interactions caused the temporary enhancement of the star-formation rate.
NGC 1436 experienced a burst of star formation between 3 to 4 Gyr ago that saw the birth of ∼50% and ∼20% of all the stars that ever formed in the inner and outer disc, respectively.

why_this_data.value: Previous ATCA HI data lacked the resolution and sensitivity to detect recent environmental interactions or recover the full single-dish HI flux; MeerKAT provides at least 10x better resolution and sensitivity.

evidence.quote: In this paper we present H I data of NGC 1436 from the MeerKAT Fornax Survey (Serra et al. 2023), whose resolution and sensitivity are at least a factor of 10 better than those of the previous ATCA H I data.

why_this_method.value: Exploiting the axisymmetry of the galaxy via elliptical annular sectors allows estimating SFH uncertainties from sector-to-sector variance rather than enforcing regularization; a multiplicative polynomial replaces two-component dust reddening due to relative flux calibration limits.

evidence.quote: However, rather than aiming at a regularized SFH solution (Cappellari 2017) we decide to exploit the axisymmetry of the system to capture the uncertainties of the SFH-reconstruction, as done earlier using MUSE data by Martinsson et al. (2018).
However, the quality of the relative flux calibration of the MUSE data is insufficient to grant such an approach, and we resort to using a multiplicative polynomial correction instead.
